rules: INSPIRE Index Polygons published in a month represent data from the previous month.
An INSPIRE monthly release remains accessible until the following month's release replaces it.
A GIS can be used to store or edit downloaded INSPIRE polygon data.
A GIS can be used to compare downloaded INSPIRE polygons with other datasets.
A GIS can be used to integrate downloaded INSPIRE polygons with other datasets.
HM Land Registry directs users to Search the index map to determine whether a piece of land is registered.
Business e-services customers can use MapSearch to view HM Land Registry's full Index Polygon dataset free of charge.
The current July 2026 INSPIRE download listing includes London Borough of Barnet.
The current July 2026 INSPIRE download listing includes London Borough of Enfield.
The current July 2026 INSPIRE download listing states that the data was published on 5 July 2026.
The current July 2026 INSPIRE download listing states that replacement files are published on the first Sunday of every month.
The current INSPIRE download page requires GIS software to view downloaded polygons.
The current INSPIRE download page requires acceptance of the Open Government Licence conditions when downloading.
The INSPIRE dataset is limited to registered freehold property rather than all tenure types.
A registered title can be represented by several separate INSPIRE polygons, so one title number does not imply one polygon.
The Planning Data documentation recommends coordinate queries for checking planning constraints at a location.
A Planning Data coordinate query can include multiple dataset parameters in a single request.
When multiple dataset parameters are supplied, Planning Data returns matching entities from any of the selected datasets.
Planning Data documents conservation-area as a dataset that can be screened at a coordinate.
Planning Data documents listed-building as a dataset that can be screened at a coordinate.
Planning Data documents green-belt as a dataset that can be screened at a coordinate.
Planning Data documents flood-risk-zone as a dataset that can be screened at a coordinate.
Planning Data documents article-4-direction-area as a dataset that can be screened at a coordinate.
Planning Data documents tree-preservation-zone as a dataset that can be screened at a coordinate.
Planning Data recommends grouping returned constraints by dataset when presenting results.
Planning Data documents fetching all 337 local planning authorities in one request with limit=500.
The all-LPA example limits returned fields to name and entity.
Planning Data documents Lambeth local planning authority entity 626195 as an example geometry_entity boundary.
The brownfield-land example uses geometry_entity with geometry_relation=within.
Planning Data documents scheduled-monument as a heritage/environmental dataset usable in UPRN screening.
Planning Data documents site-of-special-scientific-interest as a heritage/environmental dataset usable in UPRN screening.
Planning Data documents ancient-woodland as a heritage/environmental dataset usable in UPRN screening.
For raw WKT polygon queries, Planning Data requires WGS84 coordinates (EPSG:4326).
Planning Data pagination uses the offset parameter for subsequent pages.
Planning Data recommends incrementing offset by the limit value when paging.
Planning Data responses include a pre-built next pagination link.
Planning Data responses include a pre-built previous pagination link.
Planning Data responses include a pre-built first-page link.
Planning Data responses include a pre-built last-page link.
Planning Data does not provide a batch endpoint for portfolio screening.
For portfolio screening, Planning Data recommends one API request per property when using the API.
Planning Data recommends using the field parameter to limit portfolio-screening responses to needed fields.
The portfolio example limits returned fields to name, dataset and reference.
The portfolio example uses limit=50.
Planning Data explicitly recommends polite rate-limiting between property requests.
For hundreds of properties or more, Planning Data recommends bulk dataset downloads instead of repeated API requests.
Planning Data recommends running spatial intersections locally against bulk downloads for large portfolios.
Planning Data describes bulk downloads as providing a stable snapshot for large portfolio processing.
Planning Data dataset pages can provide CSV downloads.
Planning Data dataset pages can provide GeoJSON downloads.
Planning Data warns that bulk download URL formats vary by dataset.
The entity API supports a dedicated single-entity JSON representation.
The entity API supports a dedicated single-entity GeoJSON representation.
The entity API supports a dedicated single-entity HTML representation.
The dataset-list API can return JSON.
The dataset-list API can return HTML.
The dataset-list include_typologies parameter can be set false to remove typologies from JSON output.
Planning Data publishes an OpenAPI JSON description of the API.
Planning Data explicitly suggests generating a client library from its OpenAPI file using Swagger Editor.
A live Planning Data entity page can expose an authoritative quality label when data comes from an authoritative source.
Defra states that its Data Services Platform is replacing Esri Image Services with equivalent WCS and WMS services.
Defra states that WMS gives a summarised view of elevation data.
Defra states that WCS provides the underlying elevation values.
The persistent Environment Agency LIDAR Composite DTM 1m WCS endpoint omits a release-year suffix.
Environment Agency states that the yearless LIDAR Composite endpoints are intended to persist across future updates.
Environment Agency publishes a 2m last-return DSM WCS endpoint.
Environment Agency publishes a 1m last-return DSM WCS endpoint.
Environment Agency publishes a 2m first-return DSM WCS endpoint.
Environment Agency publishes a 1m first-return DSM WCS endpoint.
Environment Agency publishes a 2m DTM WCS endpoint.
Environment Agency publishes a 1m DTM WCS endpoint.
Environment Agency publishes a SurfZone DEM WCS endpoint.
Environment Agency publishes a Vegetation Object Model WCS endpoint.
Environment Agency states that WCS is an Open Geospatial Consortium standard.
Environment Agency states that WCS can serve and retrieve multidimensional coverages over the web.
Environment Agency states that WCS is usable in QGIS.
Environment Agency states that WCS is usable in Esri ArcGIS Desktop.
Environment Agency supports WCS version 2.0.1 for the elevation services.
Environment Agency describes WCS plus WMS as a non-proprietary open-format replacement for Esri image services.
Environment Agency notes compatibility issues when connecting WCS in ArcGIS and documents a workaround.
The Environment Agency ground-truth archive is updated annually according to its metadata.
The Environment Agency ground-truth dataset declares no public access constraints.
The Environment Agency ground-truth dataset is licensed under the Open Government Licence.
The Environment Agency ground-truth metadata uses EPSG:27700 as its coordinate reference system.
The Environment Agency ground-truth metadata identifier is 16b4d492-0c0d-410b-9732-65eebcc3d9f9.
The Environment Agency ground-truth dataset exposes a WMS service.
The Environment Agency ground-truth dataset exposes a WFS service.
The Environment Agency ground-truth dataset exposes an OGC API Features service.
The Environment Agency ground-truth dataset provides a file geodatabase full download.
The Environment Agency ground-truth dataset provides a GeoJSON full download.
The Environment Agency ground-truth dataset provides a GeoPackage full download.
The Environment Agency ground-truth dataset provides an Esri Shapefile full download.
The Environment Agency is the publisher of the LIDAR Ground Truth Surveys dataset.
The ground-truth metadata gives a creation date of 12 June 2019.
The ground-truth metadata gives a revision date of 12 June 2019.
The ground-truth metadata period begins on 1 January 2005.
The ground-truth metadata period ends on 1 January 2019.
Environment Agency states that all Survey Data Catalogue data is supplied in OSGB36 British National Grid.
Environment Agency states that elevations are recorded above Ordnance Datum Newlyn.
The Environment Agency LIDAR Composite is transformed using the current OSTN15/OSGM15 transformation model.
For time-stamped LIDAR and point-cloud data, Environment Agency directs users to survey metadata for the specific geoid model used.
Environment Agency states that surveys after 26 August 2016 use OSGM15.
The LIDAR Time Stamped Point Cloud metadata gives a revision date of 19 July 2024.
The LIDAR Time Stamped Point Cloud metadata period starts on 25 November 2004.
The LIDAR Time Stamped Point Cloud metadata period extends to 18 April 2024.
The LIDAR Time Stamped Point Cloud dataset offers a coverage-metadata WMS.
The LIDAR Time Stamped Point Cloud dataset offers a coverage-metadata WFS.
The LIDAR Time Stamped Point Cloud dataset provides a file-geodatabase full metadata download.
The LIDAR Time Stamped Point Cloud dataset provides a GeoJSON full metadata download.
The LIDAR Time Stamped Point Cloud dataset provides a GeoPackage full metadata download.
The LIDAR Time Stamped Point Cloud dataset provides a Shapefile full metadata download.
The Time Stamped DSM product is an archive of raster elevation data from site-specific Environment Agency surveys.
Environment Agency states that site-specific LIDAR surveys have been carried out across England since 1998.
Environment Agency notes that some areas, including coastal zones, have been surveyed multiple times.
Time Stamped DSM data can be available at 25cm resolution.
Time Stamped DSM data can be available at 50cm resolution.
Time Stamped DSM data can be available at 1m resolution.
Time Stamped DSM data can be available at 2m resolution.
The Time Stamped DSM is derived from the last-return LIDAR signal.
The Time Stamped DSM includes heights of objects such as vehicles, buildings and vegetation as well as terrain.
Time Stamped DSM rasters are supplied as GeoTIFF data in 5km zip files.
Time Stamped DSM elevation values are expressed in metres.
Time Stamped DSM elevations are referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn.
Time Stamped DSM data is aligned to the OS National Grid.
Time Stamped DSM metadata identifies the survey-specific transformation used.
OS Terrain 50 is an Ordnance Survey OpenData height product.
OS Terrain 50 is free to view for commercial, educational and personal purposes.
OS Terrain 50 is free to download for commercial, educational and personal purposes.
OS Terrain 50 is free to use for commercial, educational and personal purposes.
OS Terrain 50 is designed for landscape visualisation and analysis over large areas.
OS Terrain 50 grid and contour products are both created from the same source data.
OS Terrain 50 grid data uses regular 50m post spacing.
OS Terrain 50 contour data uses standard 10m contour intervals.
OS Terrain 50 contour data includes mean high water boundaries.
OS Terrain 50 contour data includes mean low water boundaries.
OS Terrain 50 is maintained by an integrated 3-to-5-year flying programme.
OS Terrain 50 maintenance is synchronised with other Ordnance Survey product updates.
OS Terrain 50 specifically models significant features, particularly networks.
OS Terrain 50 grid GML uses GML 3.2.1.
OS Terrain 50 grid GML uses the OGC Simple Features Profile level 0.
OS Terrain 50 provides full coverage of Great Britain.
OS Terrain 50 is designed to work with Ordnance Survey small-scale data.
OS Terrain 50 is updated annually in July.
OS Terrain 50 is based on the INSPIRE elevation specification.
Ordnance Survey verified OS Terrain 50 grid data at 4m RMSE.
OS Terrain 50 accuracy testing compared product heights with GPS points in sample areas.
OS Terrain 50 accuracy testing covers urban and major communication route areas.
OS Terrain 50 accuracy testing covers rural areas.
OS Terrain 50 accuracy testing covers mountain and moorland areas.
OS Terrain 50's GML encoding was based on the draft INSPIRE elevation specification available during product development.
OS Terrain 50 can support asset and site management applications.
OS Terrain 50 can support signal-propagation analysis.
OS Terrain 50 can support environmental analysis.
OS Terrain 50 can support high-level development analysis.
OS Terrain 50 can support geological analysis.
OS Terrain 50 can support line-of-sight planning.
OS Terrain 50 can support viewshed modelling.
OS Terrain 50 can be used as a visual aid.
OS Terrain 50 is supplied as a 50m grid in ASCII grid format.
OS Terrain 50 is supplied as a 50m grid in GML 3.2.1 Simple Features Profile level 0.
OS Terrain 50 contours are supplied in Esri Shapefile format.
OS Terrain 50 contours are supplied in GML 3.2.1 Simple Features Profile level 0.
OS Terrain 50 contours are supplied in GeoPackage format.
OS Terrain 50 contours are supplied as vector tiles in MBTiles format.
OS Terrain 50 online downloads require no registration according to the product supply documentation.
OS Terrain 50 can be downloaded in multiple formats from the Ordnance Survey Data Hub.
For ASCII, GML and Shapefile supply, OS Terrain 50 is delivered as a full Great Britain set in tiles.
OS Terrain 50 contains 2,858 10km tiles.
The 2,858 OS Terrain 50 tiles are organised into 55 folders.
Each OS Terrain 50 folder represents a 100km National Grid tile square.
OS Terrain 50 GeoPackage data is supplied as one national flat file.
OS Terrain 50 vector-tile data is supplied as one national flat file.
Grid and contour tiled supply is delivered in separate compressed folders by geographic tile.
Each compressed OS Terrain 50 tile folder contains the data plus additional supporting files.
Ordnance Survey recommends a download manager for extracting and organising the tiled OS Terrain 50 supply.
OS Terrain 50 annual updates are delivered as full tile resupply.
OS Terrain 50 grid national supply is approximately 157 MB compressed.
OS Terrain 50 downloads use ZIP compression.
OS Terrain 50 ZIP data is not encrypted.
Contour-tile compression ratios vary with the number of features in the geographic location.
OS Terrain 50 derives from the same source data as the large-scale revision programme used to update OS MasterMap Topography Layer.
OS Terrain 50 is supplied annually each July with changes made by the revision programme.
OS Terrain 50 is supplied as inert data and does not include software for data manipulation.
OS Terrain 50 may be used on hardware ranging from tablets and GIS/CAD computers to mainframes, subject to sufficient memory and storage.
A wide range of GIS software can read OS Terrain 50 GML contour data without translation.
